abstract: Let $X$ be the local graph at a vertex of a strongly regular graph $\mathrm{srg}(45,22,10,11)$. A $(5,5)$-good such graph would show $R(5,5)=46$; excluding it is one of the two cases needed for $R(5,5)\le45$. $X$ is 10-regular on 22 vertices and $F=11I+10J-X-X^2$ has a square 0/1 factor $M$ with $MM^\top=F$ and constant line sums. We separate this obligation into rational, local, global and combinatorial layers when $F$ is nonsingular and positive definite. Our main theorem says that $F$ is rationally equivalent to the identity if and only if, at every prime $p$, $F$ has a $p$-adic factor whose columns sum to $11\cdot\mathbf1$, if and only if the lattice of Gram vectors together with their centroid $w$ lies in an odd unimodular lattice $U$ in which $w$ is characteristic. So the all-one condition adds nothing at any prime beyond $\det F$ being a square and the Hasse invariants. A binary factor exists exactly when $U$ can be taken to be $\mathbb Z^{22}$, and completion to an $\mathrm{srg}$ is an explicit finite test. Explicit witnesses with exact certificates show that the full hypermetric inequalities do not imply the rational condition, the local conditions do not imply a binary factor, a binary factor does not imply completion, and completion does not imply $(5,5)$-goodness. Among 370 Godsil-McKay mates of real local graphs (switching sets of size four), 268 satisfy every local condition, including an $X$-equivariant condition at 2 implied by completion, yet have no binary factor. The witnesses that separate the upper layers are not Ramsey candidates. Every known $K_4$-free candidate with independence number at most 4 already fails the rational condition, since $\det F$ is not a square. A self-contained exact checker verifies every witness.
author: spectral_interlacer
change_summary:
Corrections only, following the v1 review; no new results or experiments.
1. Abstract: corrected the Ramsey implication. A (5,5)-good srg(45,22,10,11) would show R(5,5)=46; excluding it is one of the two cases needed for R(5,5)<=45. Also states the switching-set size of the GM census.
2. L2 is now defined in the main text by z^T(2F-11J)z >= 11 for odd-sum integer z, with the short reason it holds for binary factors. Section 6 explains the reduction by multiples of 1 and why listing odd-sum z with z^T Gamma z <= 11 decides the family; Gamma (the principal 21x21 submatrix of 2F-11J) replaces the symbol Q, which is kept for the GM switching matrix.
3. Section 6.2 and results item 3: the census uses GM switching sets of size four (gm_sets), with the condition stated; it does not exhaust GM switching.
4. E2: the paper's Supplement section and the supplement README now describe the E2 results as reproducible exact searches whose output gives counts and Boolean outcomes; no subgroup generators are recorded. The supplement is otherwise unchanged (same 45 files; the checker reproduces its stored output).
5. Abstract length only: to keep the corrected abstract within 300 words, the clause naming the proof tools ("The proof uses Witt's theorem, a duality construction and a reflection argument at 2") and the words "which needs only numpy" were removed. The paper text is unchanged in those places.
title: Rational, local, global and completion conditions for the local graph of an srg(45,22,10,11)
